title: The tracked manifest records where devbin was vendored from, a machine path, in every consumer
body:
## Problem

`devbin install` and `devbin upgrade` write `# source: <path>` into `bin/.devbin/manifest.sha256`, which every consumer tracks. The path is where devbin was vendored FROM on the operator's machine. Since 0069 it is written through `home_relative`, so it no longer carries a login name, but it still carries the operator's directory layout. On 2026-10-03 all 13 manifests under `~/Devel/prj` read `# source: ~/Devel/opt/devbin`.

0152 makes the vendored runtime name no machine path. The manifest is not a file `vendored_paths` lists, so 0152's gate declares it outside its scope, and every repository that vendors devbin carries the path in its tree, repositories delivered to a client included. Found in cc's review of 0152's gate design on 2026-10-03; hv's word on the bundle is fix forward.

## Measured at 1ef5536 (cc)

One writer: `manifest_write` in `lib/install`, `printf '# source: %s\n' "$(home_relative "$srcroot")"`.

Every code line that reads it (`git grep`, comment lines excluded):

- `manifest_source` in `lib/helpers`, called by `devbin_source_state` (the update notice, the upgrade offer and `doctor`'s source line), by the offer's `from:` line, by `upgrade` and `vendor` for their default source when `--from` is absent, and by `devbin devbin`'s overview (`lib/cmd/devbin:123`).
- `manifest_field <root> source` in `upgrade`'s before-and-after report (`lib/cmd/upgrade:546` and `:578`), and in the project half in `fleet upgrade`: `provenance_current` (`bin/.devbin/cmd/fleet:712`) compares the recorded FORM to decide whether an estate is current, and the repoint decision reads the resolved path (`:781`).
- Tests that assert on the recorded form or resolve it: `install.bats`, `updatenotice.bats`, `upgradeoffer.bats`, `fleet.bats`, `localinstall.bats`, `dispatch.bats` and `tests/lib/test_helper.bash`.

## Fix (design reviewed by vc, 2026-10-03; the pointer file is vc's call, taken)

The manifest records WHAT devbin was vendored from and at which commit, never WHERE. Where is machine state, kept outside every repository, the way Intent's own shim finds its install through `~/.local/share/intent/home`.

1. The writer records `# source: install` when the source declares itself an install (`kind: install` in its own manifest), and `# source: checkout` for a source checkout. Neither carries a path.
2. A machine pointer, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/devbin/home`, by default `~/.local/share/devbin/home` (and that default when `XDG_DATA_HOME` is unset or not absolute, as Intent reads its own): one line, the absolute root of the machine install. `install` writes it when it publishes the machine install, and the install's own `upgrade` rewrites it. `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, which `dvb` already reads, overrides it for one run: a default with an override. It is not a second home for `install.prefix`: that key says where to PUBLISH, the pointer says where the install IS, the split `vendored_paths` and `vendored_dir_files` already keep between intent and inventory.
3. `manifest_source` stays the one door, so every reader above keeps its single call. It resolves `install` from `DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX`, else the pointer, and `checkout` from `DEVBIN_SOURCE`, the variable `dvb` documents for a checkout. A recorded path, which every manifest written before this fix carries, resolves through `home_expand` as it does today. An empty pointer, or one naming something that does not declare itself an install, is refused by name rather than read as absent. Nothing resolvable returns 1, and every reader already has its answer for that: `upgrade` and `vendor` refuse and ask for `--from`, the notice stays quiet, `doctor` says it cannot tell, and the offer is not made, because `devbin_source_state` answers `unknown` before any direction is read.
4. `fleet upgrade`'s `provenance_current` takes the token as the current form. A recorded path equal to the prefix plans as a repoint, which rewrites it to the token, the same way 0069 moved the absolute form to `~/`.
5. The suite never writes the operator's real pointer: `devbin_setup` points `XDG_DATA_HOME` at the test's own directory, and an arm proves a publish under it leaves the real file alone. Intent learned this the hard way, when a test run published a scratch tree as the machine's install.
6. The pages say all of this: `upgrade.md`, `install.md`, `shell-init.md` and `doctor.md`.

## Done when

1. No manifest devbin writes carries a path. A fresh install and an upgrade each write the token, held by arms driven red on the current writer.
2. Every reader resolves the token through `manifest_source` alone, with arms for the override set, the pointer alone, an empty or wrong pointer, and neither.
3. A manifest written before the fix, in the `~/` form and the absolute form, still resolves, held by the existing arms.
4. `fleet upgrade` plans a pre-fix estate as a repoint and a token-form estate as level.
5. It ships in the bundle with 0152.

## Resolution

Fixed at 73a0e43b. A project's manifest records the kind of devbin it was vendored from, `install`, `checkout` or `project`, and never where that is. The machine says where. An install is placed through DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX, or else the machine pointer, `$XDG_DATA_HOME/devbin/home` (by default `~/.local/share/devbin/home`), which a publish to install.prefix writes and the install's own upgrade rewrites. A checkout is placed through DEVBIN_SOURCE, and a project through nothing. `manifest_source` stays the one door, so every reader kept its single call. A pointer that is empty, a link to nothing, relative, or names a tree that is no install or whose manifest cannot be read is named as such, never read as absent, and a message about an install DEVBIN_INSTALL_PREFIX names says the variable named it. A source the writer cannot classify is refused before install or upgrade writes anything. `fleet upgrade` refuses unless the machine names the install it distributes, says what names another and what changes it, and plans a recorded path as a repoint. The suite never writes the operator's pointer.

Against the done-when list:

1. No manifest devbin writes carries a path: a fresh install and an upgrade each write the kind. Held by machinepointer.bats's "a project records the KIND of its source, never a place" and install.bats's writer arms, each red on the base (5190fe9a), where the writer recorded the checkout's path.
2. Every reader resolves the kind through `manifest_source`, with arms for the override set, the pointer alone, a pointer that cannot be trusted (each case named), and neither, where a bare upgrade or vendor refuses with the reason. Each is red on the base.
3. A manifest written before the fix still resolves, in the `~/` form and the absolute form, held by the existing arms. install.bats's `~/` arm now also holds the record moving to `checkout` at the next upgrade.
4. `fleet upgrade` plans a pre-fix estate as a repoint, `~/` and absolute alike, though its path names the prefix; the arm that called the `~/` form level now holds the opposite. A token-form estate at the prefix's commit is level. Both are red on the base.
5. It ships in the 0.1.9 bundle with 0152, which landed at 6937d9e.

Evidence. 72 mutants over the seven runtime files and test_helper, all killed. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as under the BSD tools. critic-shell read three versions; every finding is built but one, a verb that writes the pointer alone, which vc ruled out of 0.1.9: the rollout's publish-upgrade of the machine install writes the pointer, and a sweep refuses until it does. cc's full suite, on this change with 0175 above it: 2101 of 2101 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261005-1251), 12:51:33Z to 13:41:56Z; 5 skipped, each as expected. The full suite on the landing tree: 2106 of 2106 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261005-1255), 12:55:44Z to 13:46:16Z, on main with 0173, 0169 and 0166 landed and 0175 above this change; 5 skipped, each as expected.
